part_a_entity_resolution.unit_of_work: one candidate pair of non-passage KG nodes (person, work, publication, concept, argument, synthesis, school, debate, position, quote, group, source_collection, controversy, event, conceptual_evolution)

same_{i}.instructions: For pairs[{i}]: a and b refer to exactly the same real-world entity (same person, same work, same publication, or same concept) -- not merely related or similar.

part_{i}.instructions: For pairs[{i}]: a is a part, section, edition, or translation of b, OR b is a part, section, edition, or translation of a (related but not strictly identical).

part_b1_school_normalization_table.method: deterministic only, no Jev call -- tallies every literal `school` string value on data/kg/nodes.jsonl (all types) and maps to the project's frozen controlled vocabulary (knowledge graph/ontology/school_scheme.json, R18) via exact match / casefold / a small synonym table
part_b1_school_normalization_table.finding: all 18 distinct raw values already equal a frozen canonical prefLabel -- 0 unmapped

part_b2_school_proposal.unit_of_work: one non-passage node of type person, work, or argument (description >= 20 chars)

school_{i}.instructions: Based only on the description of items[{i}] (an ancient/medieval person, work, or a scholarly argument about one), which philosophical school or intellectual tradition is it primarily associated with?

criteria.Stoic: Zeno, Chrysippus, Seneca, Epictetus, Marcus Aurelius; fate, providence, assent, what is up to us
criteria.Epicurean: Epicurus, Lucretius, Philodemus; atoms, the swerve, freedom from fate and from the gods
criteria.Peripatetic: Aristotle and his school (e.g. Alexander of Aphrodisias); the voluntary, deliberation, prohairesis
criteria.Academic/Platonist: Plato and the (Old/Middle/New) Academy broadly; dialogues, forms, tripartite soul, providence and fate
criteria.Middle Platonist: Alcinous, Plutarch, Numenius, Apuleius; 2nd-c. Platonism, three levels of providence/fate
criteria.Neoplatonist: Plotinus, Porphyry, Iamblichus, Proclus, Simplicius; the One, intellect, soul, providence, freedom of the soul
criteria.Pyrrhonist/Sceptic: Pyrrho, Carneades, Sextus Empiricus, Cicero reporting the Academy; suspension of judgment, arguments against fate
criteria.Presocratic: pre-Socratic Greek thinkers (Heraclitus, Parmenides, Democritus, etc.); early cosmology and necessity
criteria.Cynic: Diogenes of Sinope and the Cynic tradition; asceticism, rejection of convention
criteria.Christian (patristic): Church Fathers, Greek or Latin, 2nd-8th c. CE (apologists, Origen, Augustine, Cappadocians, etc.)
criteria.Gnostic: Gnostic teachers and texts (Valentinus, Basilides, etc.); the demiurge, hidden knowledge, dualism
criteria.Jewish: Jewish authors or traditions (Philo of Alexandria, rabbinic sources) apart from Christian patristic reception
criteria.Modern scholarship: a modern (post-1700) scholar, philosopher, or commentator writing ABOUT the ancient debate, not an ancient primary source
criteria.No school affiliation / not a school-bou: the description gives no basis for any school or intellectual-tradition affiliation
criteria.Cannot be determined from the descriptio: the description is too thin, generic, or ambiguous to decide among the above

part_b2_school_proposal.note: this 16-option list is the campaign brief's own canonical list, distinct from and not a replacement for the project's already-frozen 18-label school_scheme.json (R18); see REPORT.md

hard_rules_confirmed: no writes to data/kg/*, data/corpus/*, DB, or production
no ancient Greek/Latin generated (none of these questions ask for any)
no doctrinal-position attribution asked (libertarian/compatibilist/determinist) -- only entity identity and school/tradition
